key_insight: Neural approximation power alone does not guarantee PINN convergence; discrete stability and accurate comparison networks within admissible trial classes are also needed.
engineering_relevance: For linear elliptic Dirichlet PDEs, the framework guides collocation-point requirements and scale-dependent boundary weighting so discrete training losses can control solution error.
method: Extend kernel collocation theory to neural trial classes using elliptic regularity, discrete stability, and consistency.
Identify stable admissible subclasses and derive physics-balanced boundary weights.
Construct admissible tanh-MLP comparison networks to prove constrained convergence.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical convergence for constrained tanh-MLP residual minimization and conditional convergence for unconstrained PINNs under joint network and sampling refinement, without numerical benchmarks.
watch_item: Unconstrained convergence is conditional; low training loss or greater network capacity alone does not establish solution accuracy.
paper_title: Stable admissible neural classes and convergent physics-informed neural networks
